ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
The second phase of the 2021 Chinese Football Association Futsal Super League commenced on September 8 in Qiannan Prefecture, Guizhou Province, marking the first time the league has been held in Guizhou. The futsal field measures $40\mathrm{m}$ in length and $20\mathrm{m}$ in width, as shown in the figure. During the match, an attacking player broke through the defense $10\mathrm{m}$ from the center line and kicked the ball forward along the sideline. The motion of the ball can be considered as a uniformly decelerated linear motion on the ground with an initial velocity of $v_{1}=5\mathrm{m/s}$ and an acceleration magnitude of $a_{1}=0.5\mathrm{m/s}^{2}$. After kicking the ball, the player started chasing it with a delay of $1\mathrm{s}$, beginning from rest. His motion can be described as a uniformly accelerated linear motion with an acceleration of $a_{2}=1\mathrm{m/s}^{2}$, reaching a maximum speed of $v_{2}=6\mathrm{m/s}$, which he can maintain for an extended period.

1. At what time after the player starts chasing the football is the distance between them the greatest? What is the maximum distance?
2. How long does it take for the player to catch up to the football from the start? What is the speed of the football at that moment?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure is a rectangular five-a-side football field, with the horizontal direction labeled as 40 m and the vertical direction labeled as 20 m; in the middle there is a vertical dashed line labeled Midline; the lower boundary is labeled Sideline, and the football is drawn near the lower sideline, at a position to the left of the midline, indicating that the ball moves along the sideline direction. This position is 10 m from the midline; if it moves forward toward the opponent's goal line, the remaining field length is sufficient for checking the calculated displacement. Then reason: Let τ denote the time after the athlete starts chasing the ball. Since the athlete delays 1 s before starting to chase the ball, at this time the football has already moved for τ+1 seconds. Take the kicking point as x=0, and the forward direction along the sideline as the positive direction. The football undergoes uniformly decelerated rectilinear motion: x_b=5(τ+1)-0.5×0.5×(τ+1)^2=5(τ+1)-0.25(τ+1)^2. The athlete starts from rest and accelerates with a_2=1 m/s²; reaching the maximum speed 6 m/s requires 6 s. Therefore: when 0≤τ≤6, x_p=0.5τ^2; when τ≥6, x_p=0.5×6^2+6(τ-6)=18+6(τ-6). The distance between the two is d(τ)=x_b-x_p. Within 0≤τ≤6, d(τ)=5(τ+1)-0.25(τ+1)^2-0.5τ^2=4.75+4.5τ-0.75τ^2. Find the maximum value: d'(τ)=4.5-1.5τ; set d'(τ)=0, obtaining τ=3 s. At this time d(3)=4.75+13.5-6.75=11.5 m. The endpoints are d(0)=4.75 m and d(6)=4.75 m, so the maximum distance is indeed 11.5 m, occurring 3 s after the athlete starts chasing the ball. When catching up, first check that at τ=6 there is still d(6)=4.75 m>0, so the athlete has not yet caught up and needs to enter the uniform-speed stage. Set x_b=x_p: 5(τ+1)-0.25(τ+1)^2=18+6(τ-6). Simplifying gives τ^2+6τ-91=0; take the positive root τ=7 s. At this time the football has already moved for τ+1=8 s, and the speed is v_b=5-0.5×8=1 m/s. The displacement of the football is 5×8-0.25×8^2=24 m, which is less than the available distance from the illustrated starting point forward to the opponent's goal line, so the result is valid within the field.
